prompt: Fill in three methods whose signatures already use ? extends and ? super, then watch the tests call them with List<Integer> into List<Number>, List<String> into List<CharSequence>, and a Predicate<Object> over strings.
explanation: PECS says a structure you only read from is a Producer so it takes ? extends T, and one you only write to is a Consumer so it takes ? super T. That is exactly why copyInto can pour a List<Integer> into a List<Number> or a List<Object>: every Integer is a Number, and a list of any supertype can hold one. Predicate<? super T> follows the same rule for behaviour -- a Predicate<Object> is perfectly able to test Strings, so accepting it widens what callers may pass without weakening any type check.
hints: A for-each over List<? extends T> hands you T values directly, so `for (T item : src)` compiles with no casts.
You may add to List<? super T> but you may not read a T out of it -- which is all copyInto needs.
copyMatching is copyInto with an `if (keep.test(item))` guard around the add; count only what you actually add.
